title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step required-sequence ordering violation in an extreme-difficulty task (archived validator traces show required_command_count = 9 and changed_interface_count = 3 for that pair). We report preregistration, full execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostics for the repaired pair, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness for such workflows requires generated configurations to satisfy deterministic invariants such as required sequencing, field-level constraints, group-level availability, and syntactic well-formedness. Prior prototype systems and benchmarks illustrate feasibility and motivate verifier-aware pipelines; however, an open empirical question remains about the marginal benefit of a verifier-triggered bounded repair when the identical initial generation is deterministically reused across baseline and guarded conditions.

This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) designed specifically to isolate the marginal (repair-only) effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under those semantics the same single initial generation per task is deterministically provided to both baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator may trigger ≤1 repair) episodes. Consequently, any paired difference can only arise from deterministic validation and the single permitted repair. Our primary estimand is the paired difference in per-task binary acceptance by a deterministic verifier (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). We emphasize that this estimand is narrower than a comparison that permits independent guarded first-pass generations or multi-sample selection; it isolates the effect of the validator-triggered repair applied to a single shared candidate.
sections.related_work:
Work on intent→configuration pipelines and LLM-assisted NetOps has produced prototype systems and benchmark evaluations that motivate verifier-integrated designs. NetConfEval and related intent→config prototypes document feasibility for converting human intent into device configuration artifacts and provide benchmark-style tests for generation quality [1]. Deterministic configuration verification methods that check syntactic and semantic invariants have long been used as operational oracles for reachability, ordering, and policy compliance; such verifiers form the basis for ground-truth scoring in configuration-synthesis evaluations [2].

Adjacent literatures in program repair and generate→validate→repair loops show that validating generated artifacts against executable checks and iteratively repairing failures can improve correctness in software domains [4]. These demonstrations motivate guarded pipelines in NetOps but do not by themselves establish the empirical magnitude of repair effects for multi-device sequencing or required-sequence constraints. Research on tool-augmented LLM agents emphasizes architectural patterns—coupling generators to external solvers, validators, and execution traces—that extend capability but require careful oracle specification and artifacted evaluation to avoid overclaiming [6]. Reporting and preregistration guidance for LLM studies informed our design and archival practice [3].

Synthesis and gap addressed. The verified literature supports three relevant points: (i) intent→config pipelines are actively prototyped and benchmarked [1]; (ii) deterministic verifiers are appropriate operational oracles for many configuration correctness properties [2]; and (iii) generate→validate→repair patterns are promising but their NetOps-specific marginal effects, especially under designs that reuse identical initial candidates, are unresolved. Our paired shared_initial_candidate experiment fills the narrow empirical gap of measuring the repair-only effect when baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled generation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study design and analysis plan were preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and fixed prior to any hosted-model calls. Key preregistered elements included: (a) a paired binary estimand comparing per-task deterministic-verifier acceptance under baseline (no repair) versus guarded (verifier may trigger ≤1 repair) conditions; (b) N = 200 deterministic tasks drawn from a frozen deterministic task generator; (c) generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both episodes); (d) at most one automated repair call per task; (e) primary failed-call treatment complete_pair_primary; and (f) specified confirmatory tests (exact two-sided McNemar via exact binomial-tail) plus a paired-bootstrap percentile CI. The preregistration artifact is archived in the execution manifest.

Task generation and verifier oracle. Tasks originate from a deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) whose manifests encode initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies. The operational oracle is deterministic_netops_validator_v5: it parses generated configuration commands, enforces allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, checks required_sequence ordering constraints, evaluates group-level final_group_constraints and minimum_active_in_groups, and emits structured tracer output. Per-episode scoring uses the verifier's full_intent_constraint_validation boolean and the archived tracer fields; these tracer outputs are the authoritative evidence for scoring.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and sampling notes. The adapter contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair the exact same initial generation (a single sampled candidate) was supplied to both baseline and guarded episodes. Thus observed paired differences arise solely from validation and the single permitted repair; they cannot arise from independent guarded first-pass generations, extra sampling, prompt variants, or candidate selection. The model-configuration record declares the requested model as gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling therefore remains a possible background property even though the experiment used exactly one initial sample per pair by design.

Sanitizer and repair policy. A deterministic formatting sanitizer ran before verifier parsing. On verifier-detected violations the guarded logic could invoke at most one automated repair call to the hosted model; repair prompts were constructed deterministically from the validator trace as preregistered. Persistent unparsables after sanitizer and the allowed repair were handled per the preregistered missingness plan; the primary analysis followed complete_pair_primary.

Provider-call accounting and execution timing. Deterministic reconciliation records model-call accounting: shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1 (hosted_model_call_event_count = 201). The execution manifest records run elapsed time ≈29 minutes (start 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00, end 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00). These stage-level counts are authoritative and are reproduced in the archived deterministic_reconciliation.json artifact.

Statistical analysis. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar computed from discordant pair counts n10 and n01, implemented using the exact binomial-tail convention (p = 2 × min{BinomCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 − BinomCDF(k − 1; n, 0.5)} for n = n10 + n01 and k = n10). The paired absolute risk difference used a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples and seed = 1729 (archived). All analysis steps and seeds are recorded in the archived analysis_log.jsonl.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The run completed as preregistered with planned_episode_count = 400 and completed_episode_count = 400 (complete_pairs = 200). Provider-call accounting records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} and cache_miss_count = 201 (no cache hits). Confirmatory outcomes: baseline successes = 199, baseline failures = 1 (baseline success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200, guarded failures = 0 (guarded success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. From these counts the paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. With n = 1 and k = 1 the exact two-sided McNemar p-value (exact-binomial convention) equals p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) equals [0.00, 0.015]. These numeric results and all artifacts reproduce when the archived analysis executor is re-run on the recorded raw results (input_results_sha256 recorded in the analysis bundle).

Single repair event and diagnostic trace. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair across all pairs. Archived validator traces and the deterministic_reconciliation artifact associate this single repair with an extreme-difficulty task in the representative subset (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3, difficulty.level = "extreme"). The archived validation_before tracer fields document an ordering-violation code corresponding to a required_sequence breach; after the bounded repair the validation_after tracer shows validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied recorded in the repair trace. The repair therefore converted a sequenced-dependency failure into a configuration accepted by the deterministic verifier; the episode scorer returned score = 1 with scorer_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION". These tracer fields are the archived evidence that the single observed paired improvement resulted from a verifier-triggered bounded repair that enacted the required reordering.

Representative task difficulty distribution and exploratory diagnostics. Representative task manifests in the archived bundle show required_command_count values spanning 3–9 and changed_interface_count values up to 3 for the sampled difficulties; the lone baseline failure and the single repair both align with the higher tail of this difficulty distribution (extreme workflow compositions). This pattern is consistent with the preregistered exploratory hypothesis that multi-device sequencing and composite dependency complexity concentrate residual failures.

Missingness and contamination. The run recorded no preregistered exclusions, zero persistent unparsables, and deterministic_reconciliation indicates pair_accounting_consistent = true and all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true. No episodes have terminal errors. The provider-call audit aligns with preregistration (200 shared initial, 1 repair).
sections.discussion:
What was measured. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the same initial generated candidate was deterministically shared between baseline and guarded episodes for each task; therefore the executed estimand measures the marginal effect of permitting at most one verifier-triggered repair on that fixed candidate. The guarded condition in this experiment is not an independent guarded-first-pass generation or constrained-prompt arm; those contrasts were not executed and are outside this estimand.

Statistical regime and interpretive limits. The realized baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) places the confirmatory test in a sparse-discordant regime: only one discordant pair (n = 1) yields limited p-value sensitivity (exact McNemar p = 1.0 under the exact-binomial two-sided convention). The paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] quantifies uncertainty, placing an upper bound of 1.5 percentage points on plausible absolute improvement attributable to the repair-only estimand under the observed data and bootstrap assumptions. The preregistered power rationale had targeted detection of ~10–15 percentage-point absolute increases at N = 200 under mid-range baseline assumptions (~45–65%). The unexpectedly high baseline success rate therefore reduced realized inferential sensitivity for small repair-only effects.

Failure-mode interpretation. The single repaired pair and the lone baseline failure both occur in extreme composite-difficulty tasks characterized by long required sequences and multiple changed interfaces. The archived validator tracer for the repaired pair shows a required_sequence ordering violation (a multi-step dependency breach) that the bounded repair corrected by reordering commands according to the manifest-specified required_sequence. This is concrete, artifact-backed evidence that a verifier-triggered bounded repair can remediate certain multi-step ordering/dependency faults when those faults are expressible in the verifier's manifest-encoded invariants.

Operational implications (bounded). The artifact-grounded conclusion is narrow: in our synthetic deterministic task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a single verifier-triggered bounded repair corrected a localized ordering fault in one extreme task. This supports the claim that verifier-guided bounded repair can remedy ordering/dependency violations detectable by the verifier. It is not evidence that bounded repair would correct runtime-only omissions, vendor-specific dataplane issues, or adversarially poisoned retrieval contexts. Those remain subjects for further experiments involving live-device emulation, multi-model comparisons, independent-first-pass guarded semantics, and adversarial contamination testing.

Threats to validity. Internal: the shared_initial_candidate paired design intentionally isolates repair effects but does not address prompt sensitivity, alternative guarded prompting, or model-sampling variability beyond the single sampled initial candidate per pair. Configuration-level sanitizer behavior and repair-prompt templates are deterministic in the run but their efficacy depends on the verifier’s expressivity. Construct: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded syntactic and ordering invariants but does not substitute for dataplane emulation or vendor-specific runtime semantics. External: the experiment used a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic task bank focused on very_hard and extreme patterns; generalization to other models, broader task distributions, or production device heterogeneity is untested. Conclusion: with only one discordant pair the power to detect small repair-only effects is limited; the paired-bootstrap CI quantifies that uncertainty.
sections.conclusion: We implemented a preregistered paired experiment to measure the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. Across 200 synthetic deterministic tasks with gpt-5-mini and a deterministic verifier, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation in an extreme task. The paired absolute risk difference = 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. Artifact-grounded evidence therefore supports the constrained conclusion that verifier-guarded bounded repair can correct localized ordering faults that are expressible to the verifier in this synthetic setting. Broader operational claims require additional experiments (multi-model studies, independent first-pass guarded semantics, live-device/dataplane emulation, and adversarial contamination testing).

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier (oracle): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Archived provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are available in the execution bundle for audit.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
